tr.title: Patronun arkadaşı
tr.subtitle: E-posta · 13:05
tr.body:
Müşterilerinden birinin genel müdürü yazmış — sözleşmeye imzayı atan adamın kendisi: *"Geçen hafta bir tedarikçi yemeğinde başka bir şirketin sahibiyle konuştum, sizin üründen bahsettim. Ciddi ilgilendi — isterseniz tanıştırayım."*

E-postanın sonunda bir şart: *"Tek ricam, şu özelliği yol haritanıza almanız. İki şirket de kullanır."*

Patron seviyesinden açılan bir kapı — ama yol haritana bir borç yazıyor.

en.title: The boss's friend
en.subtitle: Email · 13:05
en.body:
The managing director of one of your customers has written — the man who signed the contract himself: *"At a supplier dinner last week I got talking to the owner of another company and mentioned your product. He was seriously interested — I can introduce you if you like."*

At the end of the email, one condition: *"My only request is that you put a certain feature on your roadmap. Both companies would use it."*

A door opened at boss level — and a debt written onto your roadmap.

_repair_note: the card is ABOUT a promise and made none; and Prospect.source has one write and no readers anywhere in the tree
_r8a_note: A non-critical interrupt is demotable (§13.2), and a demoted card lands on the desk with a clock — which is the only reason paper is a safe floor for I4. So it carries the paper trio even though it usually renders as an interrupt.
_port_note: SCOPE ADDED. Every customer-scoped effect on this card resolved to NOTHING: the old executor's default target was `get_lowest_satisfaction_customer(<event's market>)`, computed at apply time, and the port carried the effects across without carrying the default. A required slot says the same thing in the vocabulary that can also refuse the card when there is nobody to be about — which the old default could not do; it silently no-opped and the player watched a decision change nothing. LOCKS ADDED. The old builders withheld these rows by not BUILDING them — the promise row was skipped when a word was already open, the discount row when the cap was spent. A card is data now, so the row exists and must lock instead, which is §17.5's ruling and the better behaviour: a row that disappears teaches the player nothing, a row that is greyed with its reason teaches them the rule. Ported without them, every request card would have minted unlimited promises and uncapped discounts through a channel the retention card had closed.
